name: SPI read-only region write protection
description: The SPI read-only regions contain firmware data that forms part of the platform root-of-trust.
These regions must be protected from host writes after the platform has started.
This HSI attribute is vendor-neutral and may be populated by platform-specific SPI protection providers.
On Linux, fwupd may use the MTD MEMISLOCKED ioctl when the firmware flash is exposed as an MTD device.
This reports whether the current kernel-visible MTD region is write protected.
It does not prove whether the flash chip protection is hardware-pin gated, power-cycle locked, or permanent.
This is not the same as SMM BIOS Write Protect, which is a separate Intel host write control.
A future kernel API may provide stronger lock-mode information.
failure-impact: If the read-only regions are writable then an attacker may be able to modify firmware code or data that is trusted by later boot stages.

success-results.locked: SPI read-only regions are write protected

resolution: Contact your OEM, who may be able to issue a firmware update.
